children: The proposed changes target credit-life insurance commissions and volume-linked incentives, with lenders facing varying exposure based on their dependence on insurance distribution income

The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) has proposed lower commission caps for banks and non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) distributing insurance, particularly loan-linked products such as credit-life insurance. The regulator has also proposed prohibiting lenders from making insurance purchases a condition for obtaining a loan.

The proposals could affect lenders that earn fee income from insurance distribution, with the impact varying depending on their reliance on bancassurance and credit-life products. NBFCs could face greater exposure because a large share of the insurance business they source is linked to loans.

When a bank or NBFC distributes an insurance policy, it earns a commission from the insurer. This becomes particularly relevant when insurance is sold alongside a loan. Credit-life insurance covers a borrower's outstanding loan in the event of death.

IRDAI's consultation paper on ‘Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribution’ proposes product- and channel-specific commission caps. For credit-life insurance, the proposed framework would significantly reduce the payout available to distributors compared with current levels. The regulator has also proposed restrictions on compulsory bundling of insurance with loans.

The issue has gained importance as payouts on group credit-life products have increased. IRDAI said payouts on such products reached around 45 per cent in FY25, compared with around 5 per cent in FY23 when additional payouts are included. The NBFC channel also recorded Rs 10,300 crore in new business premium in FY25, up from Rs 3,600 crore in FY23, while payouts to NBFCs rose to Rs 4,300 crore. Nearly 93 per cent of the life insurance business sourced through NBFCs was group credit life.

IRDAI has also proposed changes to the bancassurance model, under which banks distribute insurance products for insurers. The regulator found that banks with multiple insurer tie-ups had average payouts of around 33 per cent, with some arrangements reaching 72 per cent, compared with 13 per cent for banks with a single tie-up. It has also proposed restricting volume-linked incentives for bank and NBFC employees distributing insurance.
The effect of the proposals is expected to vary across lenders depending on their dependence on insurance distribution income.

According to estimates cited by brokerages, bancassurance income as a proportion of FY26 income relative to FY27 normalised profit before tax (PBT) was around 2 per cent for State Bank of India, Punjab National Bank and Bank of Baroda, and around 1 per cent for ICICI Bank.

The exposure was higher among some private banks, at around 7 per cent for HDFC Bank, 9 per cent for Axis Bank, 11 per cent for AU Small Finance Bank, 17 per cent for IDFC First Bank and 18 per cent for IndusInd Bank.

Among NBFCs, JM Financial estimated insurance distribution income at around 26 per cent of FY26 PBT for L&T Finance, followed by Poonawalla Fincorp at 17.8 per cent, Cholamandalam Investment and Finance at 15.5 per cent, and HDB Financial Services and Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services at 13.4 per cent each.

The proposed changes could therefore affect both the commission income earned by lenders and the volume of insurance policies distributed alongside loans. Analysts have identified L&T Finance among the NBFCs with higher exposure to insurance distribution income.

Shares of L&T Finance fell sharply during trading on 24 September following the regulatory proposal, as financial stocks came under pressure. The stock recovered from its intraday decline but remained under pressure during the session.

The IRDAI consultation is open for comments and suggestions from stakeholders until 25 October 2026. The proposed commission and distribution changes are therefore subject to the consultation process and could be revised before any final regulations are issued.
